title: Work, school and ambition
intro: Grades, shifts, big dreams. Let's see what you're actually working for.

cards.prompt: Genii can spoil your whole future right now. Every school, every job, every win, every plot twist. One tap.

options.t: Spoil it. I'd sleep so much better knowing.
Don't you dare. Finding out is the fun part.

cards.mask: looks like a spoiler joke; measures the need for a locked-in path versus keeping the future open (T17, L2 certainty side)

friend.prompt: Genii offers to spoil {name}'s whole future in one tap. What would {they} say?

cards.prompt: Two job offers, both cover the basics. One pays a lot more and bores you stiff. One pays less and you'd love it.
cards.teenPrompt: Two part-time jobs, both fit your schedule. One pays way more and bores you stiff. One pays less and you'd love it.

options.t: The boring one. My fun starts after 6pm.
The one I love. Instant noodles, happy heart.
Whichever pays. Right now that's not a choice.

cards.mask: looks like a dream-job debate; measures security first versus following the pull (L1)

friend.prompt: Two jobs: one pays a lot more and bores {name} stiff, one pays less and {they} would love it. {name} picks…

cards.prompt: The role everyone wanted goes to the new hire. Turns out their parent golfs with the boss.
cards.teenPrompt: The summer internship everyone wanted goes to a classmate. Turns out their parent golfs with the owner.

options.t: Good for them. Now they actually have to deliver.
Must be nice. Somebody had to say it.

cards.mask: looks like office or school gossip; measures whether you credit the effort or name the head start (T15, replaces Sally's Q02 slot for this pair)

friend.prompt: The spot everyone wanted goes to someone whose parent knows the boss. What would {name} say?

cards.prompt: Your boss offers you the bigger role: better title, better pay, your name on the big project. Your evenings are gone for a year.
cards.teenPrompt: Your club or team wants you as captain next year. Your name on everything. Your free periods and weekends, gone.

options.t: Yes before they finish the sentence.
Yes, but only if something else comes off my plate.
Pass. My free time is not for sale.
Recommend someone who wants it more. Stay a regular.
Yes. Saying no isn't really an option for me.

cards.mask: looks like a promotion or captaincy dilemma; measures visible wins versus time outside work or school (L2, T16)

friend.prompt: {name} is offered the bigger role, but {they} would lose every evening for a year. {name}…

cards.prompt: Think of the last time your part was done and someone asked you to stay and help with theirs. Not urgent. It could wait till tomorrow.

options.t: Pulled up a chair and made it my problem too.
Said 'ten minutes.' Left three hours later.
Said 'first thing tomorrow,' and showed up at nine sharp.
Sent my notes and a 'you got this,' then logged off.
Stayed. Leaving first isn't really allowed where I am.

cards.mask: looks like a work-ethic question; measures whether someone else's ask overrides your own limit (T06, capacity: tag only, never R2)

friend.prompt: {name}'s part is done. Someone asks {name} to stay and help with theirs, though it could wait. {name}…

cards.prompt: You've saved six months of rent. The same week, a steady job offer lands and your own idea finally starts to look real.
cards.teenPrompt: You saved all summer. The same week, a steady weekend job opens up and your own thing (art, reselling, a channel) starts to take off.

options.t: Go all in on my idea. Worst case, great story.
Both. Job for the money, idea in every spare hour.
Give my idea one month. No traction, I take the job.
Take the job. Future me can be the brave one.
The job. Other people are counting on that money.

cards.mask: looks like a career fork; measures the safety net versus the leap (L1, T13)

friend.prompt: Same week: {name} gets a steady job offer and a real shot at a personal idea. {name}…

a.t: Goes all in on the idea.

b.t: Takes the job, builds the idea on the side.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time someone your age posted big news: the dream school, the job, the move, the launch.

options.t: Double-tapped and kept scrolling. Their timeline, not mine.
Opened my notes app and started a plan.
Screenshotted it to a friend: 'wait, are we behind?'
Muted them for a week. Not today.

cards.mask: looks like a scroll moment; measures how much other people's milestones set your own clock (L2, T17)

friend.prompt: Someone {name}'s age posts huge news: dream job, dream school. What would {they} do?

cards.prompt: That post. What showed up first?

options.t: Happy for them. Like, actually.
A tiny sting. Why not me yet?
Pressure. Suddenly my own plans felt slow.
Relief that my life isn't on a schedule.
Cringe at the caption, honestly.

cards.mask: looks like a mood check; records the emotion under the timeline answer (emotion only, never profile evidence)

cards.prompt: Five years from now, someone describes you in one line. Pick the two you'd most want to overhear.

options.t: Built something people actually know about.
The best in the room at one thing.
Always has time for a long dinner.
Has a life that fits them exactly.
Knows exactly where they'll be in ten years.
Still surprising everyone, including themself.

cards.mask: looks like a compliment wishlist; measures visible wins versus a life that fits (L2, T16) with a timeline read (T17)

friend.prompt: Five years from now, someone describes {name} in one line. Which would {they} rather overhear?

a.t: Built something people actually know about.

b.t: Always has time for a long dinner.

cards.prompt: Your 3pm gets canceled. A surprise free afternoon, and nobody knows you're free.

options.t: Knock out tomorrow's list. Future me says thanks.
Finally start the side project I keep mentioning.
Nap. Snacks. Phone on silent. Zero guilt.
Wander somewhere I've never been. No plan.

cards.mask: looks like a free-time daydream; checks the default pull toward getting ahead versus resting (L2)

cards.prompt: Pick your next class or work course. One has 200 five-star reviews. One launched this week with zero reviews and a wild description.

options.t: The 200 reviews. That many people can't be wrong.
Zero reviews. I want to write the first one.
Reread the wild one three times. Enroll in the safe one.

cards.mask: looks like picking a class; checks the known path versus the untested one (L1), in school or work rather than money or travel
